title: Normalized finite-free balancing on K-flat derived tensor models
statement: Let C, J, A, B, r and basis be as in the constant-module sheaf scalar calculus [def-sf-finite-free-scalar-calculus-data]. Given any s : FiniteFreeScalarTensorCalculus J r basis, there exists a FiniteScalarDerivedTensorModels E U s.sheaf_balance. Thus for every K in D(J,A) and N in D(J,B), U(D(E)K tensor_B N) is naturally isomorphic to K tensor_A D(U)N. On every K-flat pair P,Q there is an isomorphism U Tot(EP tensor_B Q) to Tot(P tensor_A UQ) whose component on each homogeneous summand is the specified sheaf balancing map, and whose image under Q satisfies exactly the canonical localization-tensorator square. No boundedness, constructibility or Tor conclusion is asserted.

proof.text: Given a FiniteFreeScalarTensorCalculus s, extension and restriction are exact and EP is K-flat whenever P is. For acyclic H, use the ordinary balancing of s on all homogeneous summands to identify Tot(H tensor_A UQ) with U Tot(EH tensor_B Q). Restriction preserves the sums. K-flatness of Q and exactness of E and U make this acyclic, hence UQ is K-flat. Flat-term representatives can alternatively be obtained from the existing K-flat resolution theorem and the same cancellation test proves flatness of their restricted terms.

proof.text: Using the normalized sheaf balancing of s, define the two inverse total-complex maps by their homogeneous components. They commute with the differential since the scalar has degree zero, and with arbitrary chain maps. Compute both derived tensors on K-flat pairs using the canonical localization tensorators. Descend the natural isomorphism through the two K-flat localizations. The localization equation is exactly tensor_normalized, including the mapDerivedCategoryFactors on both sides and the specified homogeneous-summand equation. Localization uniqueness gives joint naturality and independence of representatives. No constructibility or Tor interval is required.
